interpretation.G1/spec-defect: Dominant failure mode (79.8% of failures, 79.2% of all tests). The harness's expected values diverge from the implementation's outputs on ordinary inputs — evidence of a systematic expectation-generation defect rather than scattered implementation bugs.
interpretation.G3/float-edge: Second-largest group (20.0% of failures). Failures cluster at floating-point boundary values (denormals, overflow/underflow edges, rounding ties), consistent with tolerance or precision handling differences.
interpretation.G4/harness-limitation: Minimal group (6 tests, 0.2% of failures). Failures attributable to limitations of the test harness itself rather than the implementation under test.
interpretation.G2: No tests classified into G2 — this root-cause group is unrepresented in the current triage.

coverageGaps: G2 root-cause group has zero members; if G2 corresponds to a plausible failure mode (e.g. environment/driver differences), no test currently exercises it.
Only 16 of 2598 tests pass (0.62%); with G1 dominating, the expectation-generation pipeline should be audited before drawing per-test conclusions from G3/G4 classifications.
